subject: Television & Streaming
title: Milton Berle: Mr. Television
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Milton Berle: Mr. Television.

hook.text: In 1948, Tuesday nights in America went silent. Restaurants emptied. Milton Berle was on TV.

buildup.text: NBC gave Berle a variety show. He wore wild costumes, threw pies, and mugged for the camera with manic energy.

discovery.text: Appliance stores reported TV sales spiked on Wednesdays—the day after Berle's show aired.

twist.text: Critics called his humor crude and childish. But 80 percent of all TV viewers tuned in every week.

climax.text: Berle proved one thing: a single show could make an entire nation buy television sets.

punchline.text: One comedian sold more TVs than every ad combined.

quiz.question: What earned Milton Berle the nickname 'Mr. Television'?
options: His show drove millions of Americans to buy television sets
He hosted the first color broadcast
